items.text: Saint-Martin (French part) is an overseas collectivity of France. France's national drug penalties are: Using any narcotic, cannabis included, is banned even in private and for recreation. The usual response is a fixed fine of EUR 200 (about A$318 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293); a court can impose up to 1 year in prison and EUR 3,750 (about A$5,959). Service-Public's page is written for France as a whole; it does not say how each collectivity applies it.

Under Article 74 of the French Constitution each overseas collectivity has its own statute that sets out how national law applies there. Which parts of the drug-use rules apply here has not been confirmed from the statute.
